ops.title: 2026-07-03 NFS-cutover CPU spike root causes — holder Darwin BG band (fixed fusekit v0.27.0, nice 5) + silly-rename privacy leak (holderfs diversion, v0.28.0); a self-set BG band is externally unclearable
ops.body:
The 2026-07-03 fleet re-fuse (all 10 accounts → fuse-t NFS) melted under load: claude sessions
at ~440% CPU, load 25, wedged/dead mirrors. Two root causes, both fusekit-side:

1. **Darwin BG band on the holder** (since fusekit v0.23.0): holder + inherited go-nfsv4
   servers ran PRI 4 vs claude's 31 — the mounts' data plane was CPU+I/O-throttled below the
   sessions it served. Measured: 1.4–3.4 ms open/close vs ~214 µs normal-priority control
   floor. **A self-set band cannot be cleared from outside** — `taskpolicy -B` and
   `setpriority(PRIO_DARWIN_PROCESS, pid, 0)` return success with NO effect (verified via
   scratch self-BG process); restart-only. Fixed in fusekit **v0.27.0**: `proc.Nice(5)`
   (soft weight, no I/O demotion; nice is one-way for unprivileged processes). Holder cask
   0.27.0 published; deploy needs a zero-live-session window (cc-pool backlog task ff181f3).
2. **Silly-rename privacy leak**: fuse-t handles unlink/rename-over of an open file via
   `Rename(x → /.fuse_hiddenN)`; holderfs mapped the target into SHARED base, so the
   account-PRIVATE merged .claude.json landed in ~/.claude readable via every account's mount
   (4 × ~489 KB in 13 min). Fix: holderfs diverts the silly-rename class (.fuse_hidden/.nfs.)
   to privateRoot + readdir suppression + Build sweep — fusekit **v0.28.0**, VM-gated.

attrcache stays NEVER (torn reads at any TTL — [[carveout-regression-v0363]]); cc-pool pins it
with TestOverlaySpecNeverOptsIntoAttrCache. ccn docs: fusekit 130274e (mechanism
contraindications), cc-pool bdf2768 (incident chronology). Residual by design: ~200 µs/op
loopback-NFS floor; next lever is negative-lookup caching (nonegnamecache — no fuse-t knob,
upstream ask). Related: [[macos-nfs-vinvalbuf2-panic]], [[fusekit-content-over-rpc]].
